title: India's consumer economy is moving toward AI-assisted, transparent, connected commerce where governance and resilient supply chains become part of competitive advantage
source_unit: Deloitte India and FICCI, Consumer trends IGNITEing growth and governance
geography: India FMCG, retail, and e-commerce sectors

denominator.unit: US dollars; projected size of India's consumer economy by 2030

consumer_economy.unit: trillion US dollars projected consumer-economy size by 2030

growth_drivers.value: AI use, resilient operations, connected commerce, differentiated experiences, regulatory predictability, and digital trust

observations.method: Deloitte India-FICCI report summary and quoted outlook in the official Deloitte press release; the figure is a projection, not an observed current market size.
observations.uncertainty: The public release does not provide the full projection model, scenario assumptions, sector weights, or distributional effects; aggregate market growth does not establish household welfare or equal access.
observations.subgroup: Indian consumers, FMCG firms, retailers, e-commerce platforms, brands, regulators, and supply-chain workers.
observations.counterinterpretation: A larger consumer economy can coexist with affordability pressure, unequal digital access, labor displacement, concentrated platform power, and environmental costs.

denominator.unit: Deloitte India-FICCI consumer-trends report sample and method as described in the public release

nutrition_information_review.unit: percent of consumers reported as reviewing ingredient or nutritional information before purchase

formulation_choice.unit: percent of consumers reported as choosing products based on formulations and ingredients

brand_switching.unit: percent of consumers reported as switching brands for better health and transparency credentials

observations.method: Consumer measures reproduced from the official Deloitte press-release summary of the report's six structural trends.
observations.uncertainty: The public release does not state sample size, field dates, weighting, question wording, market coverage, or whether responses are representative of India's population; percentages should not be generalized beyond the report's defined sample.
observations.subgroup: Consumers making FMCG and related purchase decisions, especially those evaluating health, ingredient, formulation, and transparency claims.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stated information-seeking or switching behavior may not become actual purchases when prices, availability, household budgets, habit, or trust in labels constrain choice.

ecommerce_projection.unit: billion US dollars; projected Indian e-commerce market by 2030, approximately

quick_commerce_projection.unit: billion US dollars; projected Indian quick-commerce market by 2030

commerce_shift.value: Retail, e-commerce, quick commerce, omnichannel, and creator-led ecosystems are blurring channel boundaries for discovery, evaluation, purchase, and fulfilment

observations.method: Official Deloitte press-release summary of the report's commerce and channel trends; projections are reported estimates.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not specify projection assumptions, definitions of e-commerce or quick commerce, geographic coverage, profitability, worker conditions, or consumer-cost effects.
observations.subgroup: Urban and non-urban consumers reached by digital commerce, creators, retailers, delivery workers, brands, logistics firms, and platform operators.
observations.counterinterpretation: Convenience and personalization can increase delivery intensity, packaging, surveillance, impulse spending, and dependence on platform-mediated access while leaving offline retail and excluded households behind.

observations.period: 2026; governance, sustainability, and trust in consumer markets

sustainability_consideration.unit: percent of consumers reported as considering sustainability in purchase decisions

governance_scope.value: data privacy, AI governance, sustainability, product quality, and consumer protection are described as embedded in business strategy

supply_chain_shift.value: Supply chains are described as moving from efficiency optimization toward resilience through intelligent planning, predictive forecasting, and diversified sourcing

observations.method: Official Deloitte press-release summary of the report's governance, sustainability, and supply-chain findings.
observations.uncertainty: The public release does not establish whether reported sustainability consideration changes purchases or emissions, or whether governance commitments produce enforceable consumer remedies and worker protections.
observations.subgroup: Consumers, firms, regulators, suppliers, logistics workers, communities exposed to production and delivery systems, and users of data-driven commerce.
observations.counterinterpretation: Governance and sustainability can become compliance or marketing layers while costs are passed to consumers, small suppliers, workers, or communities without measurable accountability.

boundary: This record adds an India consumer-economy signal on AI-assisted discovery, transparency-led choice, connected commerce, resilient supply chains, governance, sustainability, and globalizing Indian brands. It uses the official Deloitte press-release summary of a Deloitte India-FICCI report; it is not a representative national survey, a complete market census, a causal evaluation, or proof that stated consumer preferences become realized purchasing power or improved welfare.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Deloitte India press release reviewed for the projected consumer-economy scale, consumer decision percentages, commerce projections, sustainability measure, AI and supply-chain claims, and governance framing.
